title: Scandinavian Defence
intro: Black answers 1.e4 with 1...d5 at once and takes back with the queen. Simple to learn and solid, with a clear plan.

lessons.title: The main line with Qa5
lessons.summary: Hit e4, take back with the queen, then tuck it on a5.

steps.text: 1...d5 attacks the e4 pawn straight away. After 2.exd5 Qxd5 the queen is out early, and 3.Nc3 chases it with tempo.
The queen goes to a5: away from the knight, out of the centre, and still eyeing e1 and the knight on c3. Then Black develops with ...Nf6, ...c6 and ...Bf5, a sturdy position with an easy plan.
Play the main line as Black.
steps.hint: d5, take back with the queen, then queen to a5, knight to f6 and pawn to c6.
steps.ifRight: That is the Scandinavian main line. Next comes ...Bf5 and ...e6.

steps.text: White develops the bishop towards f7 with 6.Bc4.
Bring your light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before playing ...e6.
steps.hint: Put the c8 bishop on f5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Bf5 so your bishop stays active outside your pawns.
steps.ifRight: Now ...e6 will not trap your bishop.

feedback.e7e6: 6...e6 locks in your c8 bishop. Get it out first with 6...Bf5.

steps.text: White lines up a discovered attack on your queen with 7.Bd2. Finish opening the way for your dark-squared bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...e6: if 8.Nd5, your queen simply drops back to d8.
steps.ifRight: Black has a rock-solid, harmonious position.

lessons.title: Where the queen and pieces go
lessons.summary: Retreat safely against Nd5, recapture with the queen, and finish development.

steps.text: White often jumps in with 8.Nd5, threatening your queen with a discovered attack and eyeing f6.
Move your queen to safety without losing a pawn.
steps.hint: Return the queen home to d8.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8...Qd8 so d8 guards c7 and keeps everything protected.
steps.ifRight: Your queen is safe and White must deal with the knight on d5.

feedback.a5a4: 8...Qa4 lets White play 9.Nc7+ and win a rook.

steps.text: Recapture cleanly without damaging your kingside pawns.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9...Qxf6 to keep your kingside pawns healthy and develop smoothly.
steps.ifRight: Your queen stands actively on f6, eyeing d4 and the kingside.

feedback.g7f6: 9...gxf6 weakens your kingside pawns. Take back with 9...Qxf6.

steps.text: White develops 10.Qe2 to prepare O-O-O and threaten d5.
Develop your last minor piece or prepare castling.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to d7 or dark-squared bishop to d6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 10...Nd7 (or 10...Bd6): Black finishes development and can castle either side.
steps.ifRight: Black has a very solid position with zero weaknesses.
